title: Navigating a New World Order- Macro Strategies for Uncertain Times - Pablo Calderini

speakers: Pablo Calderini (President and CIO, Graham Capital Management)
Chief client officer (host, name garbled in captions)
summary: Graham Capital client session (Jan 2023 context): post-GFC policy regime ended, hiking-cycle history, core inflation and changing stock-bond correlation justify macro as a complement to 60/40 with positive skew and negative conditional correlation. Describes quant trend and quant macro programs and tactical views.

coverage.note: Graham intro; post-GFC accommodative regime vs inflation shock
Inflation not secular low; five hiking cycles; current cycle record; method of forward curves
Forward curve vs delivered; core vs energy inflation
Core persistence; stock-bond correlation regimes; stocks for the long run
Long-horizon variance; macro conditional correlation and skew
20% macro in 60/40; Treasury 20 sigma; macro as complement
Current views: short equities, long EUR, JPY, gold
Quant side: trend and quant macro sub-strategies
Quant macro track and comparison with trend

completeness_estimate: 0.86 - first reader captured nearly every argument of the slide-by-slide talk (hiking cycles, core inflation, stock-bond correlation, long-horizon variance, macro skew); missed a few supporting causal links and operating details (inflation drives correlation, Fed guidance blamed, concentrated multi-PM book, recency bias).

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: there was not one crisis that the FED uh was not able to accommodate
claims.claim: For ten years after the GFC every shock was met by very accommodative central banks (zero lower bound, sticky-low inflation), a special regime that is over after the 2022 inflation shock.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: it's a shock that needs to be matched by another shock
claims.claim: The inflation shock must be met by a shock to real rates, so asset markets and central banks play a completely different game from the post-GFC decade.
claims.testable: partly: real rate shocks versus asset returns

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: inflation is not that sticky low central banks can do whatever they want with their balance sheets
claims.claim: Inflation is no longer seen as a secular low (supply disruptions, geopolitics, fiscal expenditure), so central banks will be shyer about accommodative policy, leading to higher volatility and a harder time for 60/40.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the last five hiking Cycles uh since post Volker
claims.claim: Of the last five hiking cycles since Volcker (1994-95 +300bp, 1999-2000 +175bp, 2005-06 +425bp, 2015-18, plus 2022), each ended with a crisis or turmoil (tequila, Asia, Nasdaq, GFC, 2018) after which the Fed gave up.
claims.testable: yes: event study of hiking cycle ends

correction.issue: Overstated: the 'five cycles' are four completed cycles (1994-95, 1999-2000, 2005-06, 2015-18) plus the still-running 2022-23 cycle; only the four completed cycles ended in turmoil, and the 2015-18 cycle ended with turmoil in 2018 while the cut came in March 2020 with covid.
correction.fix: In the four completed hiking cycles since Volcker (1994-95 +300bp, 1999-2000 +170-175bp, 2005-06 +425bp, 2015-18) the Fed stopped after turmoil (tequila and Asian crises, Nasdaq collapse, the global financial crisis, 2018 market turmoil); the current cycle is a fifth, still running.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the current height is double the average of the previous four hiking Cycles
claims.claim: The 2022-23 hiking cycle is a record in magnitude and speed: double the average of previous four cycles (about 220bp) in half the time, heading to about 500bp.
claims.indicator: Fed hiking cycle size and speed

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: let's see how forward curves were on
claims.claim: Method: compare the forward curve on the first day of each hiking cycle with what the Fed delivered to judge how prepared (fragile) markets were; the less priced, the more fragile.
claims.indicator: forward curve at first hike versus delivered

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the FED actually did a fairly good job at least for the first 18 months always in guiding markets really well to what was to come
claims.claim: In earlier hiking cycles forward pricing was close to what the Fed delivered for 18 months, so markets were well prepared and resilient.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the FED height 300 basis points more than what the markets were pricing
claims.claim: In 2022 the Fed hiked about 300bp more than the forward curve priced at the first hike, a huge unprecedented shock to markets and a reason for fragility.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: if we are in a deflationary period higher inflation actually can be very positive for asset prices
claims.claim: The beta of asset returns to inflation is non-linear: higher inflation helps in deflation and hurts in high inflation, which is why regression coefficients look inconclusive.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: core inflation as always a massive negative shock for us at prices while NRC or headline inflation X score uh being almost unimportant
claims.claim: A Wharton study splitting inflation by drivers finds core inflation is a large negative shock for asset prices while energy/headline ex-core is nearly unimportant, because energy inflation is volatile and mean-reverting.
claims.direction: bearish equities on core inflation surprises
claims.testable: yes: replicate with core vs energy

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: it will entice a much a much bigger response by asset prices
claims.claim: Core inflation is persistent (rises stay) so it needs a larger policy response and causes a larger asset price reaction than energy inflation.
claims.testable: yes: autocorrelation of core vs energy

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: it's once were correlated to equities you would have almost no bonds in your portfolio
claims.claim: Bonds are held because their lower expected return buys a hedge; with a 400-500bp equity risk premium they only make sense with a low or negative correlation to stocks.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the long run correlation between stocks and bonds is really around zero
claims.claim: The long-run stock-bond correlation is about zero, an average of periods of high positive and high negative correlation; it was very positive from the 1960s to 2000s in high-inflation periods.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: it's hard to think we're going to go back to the the great days of minus 50 correlation between stocks and bonds
claims.claim: Going forward stock-bond correlation is expected near zero, not the -0.5 of the previous 20 years that made 60/40 a bonanza.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: stocks for the long run
claims.claim: The 'stocks for the long run' argument relies on mean reversion and lower long-horizon variance, but variance forecasts forward must also estimate the unknown mean.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: when you do proper calculations stocks are a lot more volatile in the long run
claims.claim: Without the degree of freedom from a known mean, proper long-horizon calculations raise equity volatility from about 17% to about 22%, so mean-variance should hold fewer equities.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: are also not the diversifiers that they were
claims.claim: Bonds with low returns and zero correlation to stocks in a period of active monetary policy are not the diversifiers they were.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the conditional correlation I our correlation to equities when equities are doing really badly it's negative
claims.claim: Macro funds (HFRI macro index) have zero average correlation to equities but negative conditional correlation, gaining in large equity drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we have that so-called positive skew which means that we tend to if we're gonna surprise you we're gonna surprise you on the upside
claims.claim: Macro returns show positive skew (almost 4 sigma on the upside, no -3 sigma), valuable for portfolio construction.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: skewness and conditional correlation are super important
claims.claim: Investors focus too much on Sharpe, returns and standard deviation; skewness and conditional correlation should enter efficient portfolio construction.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: adding 20 macro might actually will actually cut the annual return a bit but we'll cut the volatility a lot more
claims.claim: Adding 20% macro to a 60/40 over the last 20 years lowers return slightly but lowers volatility more, lifting information ratio from 0.66 to 0.75 and cutting worst drawdown from -36% to -29%.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: what happened in threshold yields was uh really is 20 Sigma event
claims.claim: The March 2023 Treasury yield move was a 20 sigma event that hurt dynamic trading funds; Graham was little affected but is making risk systems more robust to such shocks.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we see it as a complement to the 60 40 portfolio we don't we don't hold very long term secular views
claims.claim: Macro is a complement to 60/40: it holds no long-term secular views (already in 60/40) and adds value by being tactical, dynamic and quick to cut positions when the thesis fails.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we are we are short equities uh we were not short on the way up
claims.claim: Short equities: earnings must fall and multiples are too high; either sticky core inflation forces the Fed to hike versus priced cuts, or core falls only via unemployment spike and recession cutting earnings; views are changeable.
claims.indicator: S&P earnings, multiples, fed funds futures pricing cuts

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we actually like the Euro we feel that with the banking issues in the U.S
claims.claim: Long euro: US banking issues stop the Fed from hiking massively while the ECB is hawkish.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: Ian is extremely extremely undervalued so we we like Yen as well
claims.claim: Long yen: extremely undervalued and a BoJ yield-curve-control change eventually coming.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we like gold I mean that's the one that we have the most conviction
claims.claim: Long gold, highest conviction: real rates are elevated and will come down, breakevens are too low, and the US debt ceiling negotiation is usually gold-bullish.
claims.testable: yes: gold vs real rate and breakeven changes

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we can talk in a month and have completely different views
claims.claim: Discretionary macro value is the ability to change views and positions within a month rather than stick to a view.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we do bring in fundamental data points into that font macro signal
claims.claim: Quant macro blends price-based signals with fundamental data, giving a more dynamically evolving positioning than pure trend.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: this passage is the host (Graham chief client officer) summarising the systematic side, not Pablo Calderini; the transcript says pure trend is price-driven and the quant macro strategy brings in fundamental data points.
correction.fix: The host (chief client officer) says Graham's pure trend following is price-driven while the quant macro strategy adds fundamental data to the price signal, so its positioning can evolve more dynamically.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we have added value on top of trend
claims.claim: Trend program adds value via robust portfolio construction (mean-variance, PCA to estimate covariance matrix fast to mitigate risk) on a traditional time-series momentum signal.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: one is based on on on Trend the other one is based on value or long-running reversion the other one is based on Curry
claims.claim: The quant macro program has four sub-strategies: trend, value (long-run reversion), carry and macro fundamentals, combined by mean-variance; running eight years with Sharpe above one.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: it's highly non-linear it depends on what regime you're on
claims.claim: Fundamentals affect markets non-linearly and regime-dependently, so the macro signal uses about 900,000 time series, NLP sentiment and data compression with non-linear regression.
claims.indicator: GDP, inflation, earnings, inventories, NLP sentiment

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we try to come up with ideas of equilibrium of required cover
claims.claim: Carry is not naive: they avoid simply buying high-carry assets and estimate an equilibrium required carry.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: Trend following has a very nice negative conditional correlation to equities when equities tank
claims.claim: Trend gains when equities tank; the quant macro program has less of that conditional benefit but a more stable return profile and higher information ratio than trend.
claims.indicator: trend vs quant macro conditional correlation

claims.speaker: Chief client officer (host)
claims.quote: rather than have 50 or 150 teams here we have roughly 15 today
claims.claim: Graham runs its discretionary multi-PM macro book concentrated, betting on its highest-conviction teams (about 15) rather than spreading across 50 to 150 teams, a portfolio-construction choice favouring conviction over breadth.
claims.testable: partly - needs PM-level returns to compare concentrated and diversified multi-PM books

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: I would put the culprit on the on the FED right I would say by how badly the FED building guiding markets to to the actual outcome
claims.claim: The 2022 hiking shock was a Fed communication failure: in past cycles good forward guidance (or good market reading) left markets resilient, whereas in 2022 the Fed hiked far beyond what it had guided, producing a larger shock to asset prices.
claims.indicator: forward curve at first hike versus realised Fed path
claims.conditions: larger gap between priced and delivered hikes means more fragility
claims.testable: yes - compute priced-minus-delivered path for each cycle and relate to subsequent drawdowns

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: High inflation usually drives correlation up
claims.claim: High inflation pushes the stock-bond correlation up (to positive) because inflation shocks hit both assets; a falling-inflation regime gives negative correlation, so the sign of the correlation follows the inflation regime.
claims.indicator: rolling stock-bond correlation versus inflation level
claims.direction: stock-bond correlation rises when inflation is high
claims.conditions: high-inflation regimes such as the 1960s-1990s; zero or near zero in 2022-23
claims.testable: yes - rolling correlation against CPI regimes

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we have lived in this world of negative correlation for 20 years now to the point that I think that new newcomers to financial markets might
claims.claim: After 20 years of negative stock-bond correlation, newer market participants assume bonds always hedge stocks, an extrapolation of a regime that is not the long-run norm, which leaves 60/40 portfolios exposed when the sign flips.
claims.testable: partly - the 20-year negative-correlation fact is testable, the belief claim is not

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: I also think these are our asses like we saw last year when things get really bad I think macro has the capacity to even improve on this right
claims.claim: The 20-year average benefit of adding macro to 60/40 understates the benefit in stress years such as 2022, when macro can add more than the average.
claims.indicator: 60/40 plus macro portfolio in stress years
claims.testable: yes - split the sample by 60/40 drawdown years

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: cognizant though that there's Market forces supporting equities that are beyond our understanding and that's where it comes our uh our risk management and our tactical head
claims.claim: A fundamental short-equity view is held with humility: unknown market forces may keep equities supported, so risk management and a tactical hedge are used to limit the cost of being early or wrong.
claims.direction: short equities with tactical risk control
claims.conditions: fundamental view contrary to price action

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: one is a trend following program right and that did really well last year
claims.claim: Graham's trend-following program did really well in 2022, the year of the inflation shock and rate-hike regime, consistent with trend profiting from large macro dislocations.
